sources.title: Gemini 3 Pro Model Card (May 2026 update)
sources.evidence: Reopened the complete May 2026 card on October 27, 2026. Page 2 explicitly says Gemini 3 Pro is not a modification or fine-tune of a prior model; it identifies subsequent 3-series variants as descendants. Page 3 describes sparse MoE routing qualitatively, without total size, expert dimensions, routing width or a numerical active count. No parameter-size disclosure appears in the remaining card.

sources.title: Gemini 3 Pro preview — Gemini API
sources.evidence: Exact model code gemini-3-pro-preview; input limit 1,048,576, output limit 65,536; text/image/video/audio/PDF inputs and text output; thinking and function calling supported. Links the Gemini 3 Pro model card. Explicitly says the endpoint was shut down March 9, 2026; page updated August 18, 2026. Reopened October 27, 2026: the exact endpoint specification still contains no total or activated parameter count; the current page update is October 27.

sources.title: Start building with Gemini 3
sources.evidence: November 18, 2025 announcement says Gemini 3 Pro is available in preview through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio and Vertex AI, and describes reasoning, coding and multimodal understanding. Reopened October 27, 2026; capabilities and benchmark comparisons contain no total/active count or count-bearing base relationship.

sources.title: Gemini deprecations
sources.evidence: The exact gemini-3-pro-preview row records release November 18, 2025 and shutdown March 9, 2026, with gemini-3.1-pro-preview as replacement. The image-preview variant is a separate row with a different release date.

sources.title: Gemini 3.1 Pro Model Card
sources.evidence: Fresh complete-card review October 27, 2026. Its named Gemini 3 Pro dependency is explicit, but its exact Gemini 3 Pro comparison column reports benchmark scores rather than parameter size. No numerical total or activated count appears.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon Model Card
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27, 2026 inspection of the complete decoded current card. It gives no numerical total or active count for Gemini 3 Pro. Argon is itself explicitly a new model rather than a modification or fine-tune; its separate specifications are not transferred backward.

sources.title: Gemini API Additional Terms of Service
sources.evidence: Provides proprietary service terms for Gemini API and AI Studio. Read together with the original model card distribution section, this supports a proprietary classification rather than a released-weight license. The currently displayed terms are effective March 23, 2026; no historical term version is asserted.

sources.title: Empty shelves or lost keys? Recall is the bottleneck for parametric factuality
sources.evidence: Reopened October 27, 2026. The August 12 Google Research post studies Gemini-3-Pro knowledge encoding and recall, not model size. Followed its linked research paper and inspected parameter references and model-comparison tables; no total or active count is disclosed.

sources.title: Models.dev Gemini 3 Pro Preview record
sources.evidence: Followed the baseline catalog link. It supplies the gemini-pro grouping and repeats the preview identity and API limits; technical claims were independently checked against Google sources.

sources.title: Gemini 4 Argon Safety and Security Report
sources.evidence: Fresh October 27, 2026 inspection of the full report text and every parameter/Gemini 3 Pro occurrence. Retrospective comparisons cover biological-risk evaluations, persuasion, situational awareness and other safety measures, not total or active model sizes. Parameter mentions concern security, encoded knowledge and a task-difficulty variable.

sources.title: Empty Shelves or Lost Keys? Recall Is the Bottleneck for Parametric Factuality
sources.publisher: Calderon et al.; linked by Google Research
sources.evidence: Followed from the first-party Google Research post on October 27, 2026 and read the full HTML after the web reader timed out. Gemini-3-Pro comparisons measure factual encoding and recall. The numerical model-size discussion concerns the Gemma family, not Gemini 3 Pro; no total or active Gemini count is given.

sources.title: Distilling Answer-Set Programming Rules from LLMs for Neurosymbolic Visual Question Answering
sources.publisher: Higuera Ruiz, Oetsch and Eiter; Cambridge University Press
sources.evidence: Fresh exact-model search surfaced a 1-trillion count. Downloaded and inspected page 17 on October 27, 2026: the paper explicitly calls this an estimate, without a derivation or parameter-specific developer citation. Footnote 12 links the generic Google Pro page, which currently describes Gemini 3.1 Pro and has no parameter count. This application paper is a discovery lead, not a Google specification.

sources.title: Google's TPU v6e production ramp — inside the Council Bluffs cluster
sources.evidence: Fresh count search found claims of 1.6T total and 280B active. Opened the page October 27, 2026: it labels itself AI-generated and provides no linked developer evidence for those figures. Its claimed March 10, 2026 Gemini 3 Pro launch contradicts the original November 18, 2025 announcement. Both numbers remain unsupported and are not adopted.

sources.title: Gemini Pro product page
sources.evidence: Followed the Cambridge paper footnote on October 27, 2026. The live page describes Gemini 3.1 Pro and compares it with Gemini 3 Pro using benchmark scores. It gives neither a total nor active count, so it does not substantiate the paper’s 1T estimate.

sources.title: Gemini 3.5 Flash Model Card
sources.evidence: Fresh complete-card review October 27, 2026. This descendant names Gemini 3 Flash as its base and links earlier cards for architecture. Its comparisons supply performance and safety values, not a retrospective total or activated-parameter disclosure for Gemini 3 Pro.

parameters_b.note: Fresh October 27 exact-model count and lineage searches, original evidence and later primary comparisons found no supported nominal total. The original card explicitly excludes modification/fine-tuning of a prior model, so no known-size base is identified. The Cambridge paper labels 1T an estimate; its generic Google citation supplies no count. The AI-generated INTELAR 1.6T claim lacks developer provenance. Retain null because numerical evidence is absent, not because an exact tensor census is required.

INTELAR’s unsupported 280B claim is not adopted; performance, capacity estimates and sibling lineage do not supply an active count.

patch.notes: Sparse MoE Transformer; Google identifies Gemini 3 Pro as a new model, not a fine-tune of an earlier one. Total and active parameter counts are undisclosed. Context and capabilities describe the retired gemini-3-pro-preview endpoint, shut down March 9, 2026. Distinct from Gemini 3 Pro Image and Gemini 3.1 Pro.

research_notes.exact_identity: The Google API page explicitly links this preview endpoint to the Gemini 3 Pro model card. Original preview release and retirement are independently listed in the official lifecycle table.
research_notes.parameter_and_architecture_checks: Fresh October 27 exact-name/ID searches covered total, active, activated, billion/trillion and named-base evidence. Reopened the original May-updated card, exact API and launch; inspected later 3.1 Pro, 3.5 Flash, Argon and Gemini 4 safety comparisons, plus Google Research and its linked factuality paper. No supported numerical size emerged. The original card explicitly says this model is not a modification or fine-tune of a prior model. Investigated and rejected the Cambridge 1T estimate and INTELAR 1.6T/280B claims for lack of developer support.
research_notes.access_limitations: The old Vertex AI /models/gemini/3-pro URL redirects to a general Google-models page. The Gemini API exact-model page remains accessible and supplies the historical specifications. No live inference request was made.

summary: October 27 parameter re-audit retains explicit null total and active counts after fresh searches, original evidence, later primary comparisons and research checks. The original card identifies a new model rather than a prior-model fine-tune. Traced numerical leads to an explicitly estimated application-paper count and unsupported AI-generated reporting. Preserved all unrelated field assessments and corrections.
